sentences: I measure the board twice with a tape measure and mark the cut line with a pencil.
I clamp the piece to the workbench and check that it does not move before sawing.
I sharpen the chisel on a whetstone until the edge cuts paper cleanly.
I cut the dovetail pins with a fine-tooth saw and then remove the waste with a chisel.
I spread wood glue on both surfaces and press them together for thirty seconds.
I sand the surface with 120-grit paper, then switch to 220-grit for a smoother finish.
I drill pilot holes before driving the screws to prevent the wood from splitting.
I check the squareness of the corner by comparing the diagonal measurements of the frame.
I plane the edge of the board until it is straight and flat against the straightedge.
I select a piece of maple from the rack and inspect it for knots and cracks.
I apply a coat of tung oil with a rag and wipe off the excess after ten minutes.
I use a marking gauge to scribe a line parallel to the edge of the workpiece.
I assemble the mortise and tenon joint and tap it together with a mallet.
I set the router bit depth and run the profile along the edge of the tabletop.
I turn a bowl on the lathe, checking the thickness with calipers as I go.
I countersink the screw heads so they sit flush with the surface of the wood.
I stack the cut pieces in order and label each one with a pencil mark.
I check the level of the assembled cabinet and adjust the feet until it sits flat.
I remove the clamps after the glue dries and scrape off the squeezed-out residue.
I vacuum the sawdust from the workbench and put the hand tools back on the rack.
